### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **87** documentable anchor(s).

**88** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0cd594b3c77d7e5ac5be02b4c284c5ad5cd1009c`.

⛔ **17** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `routeManager (25 routes)`, `resolveProtocol (29 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/meta/:type/:name (route, 43 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **69** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0cd594b3c77d7e5ac5be02b4c284c5ad5cd1009c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ccf5abeda0f2993587a7b0bdb6d6766cd00aef40` — the merge of head `35e5d2ce273f89af436131c7deaa6f7361e18dc1` into base `0cd594b3c77d7e5ac5be02b4c284c5ad5cd1009c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ccf5abeda0f2993587a7b0bdb6d6766cd00aef40 && git checkout ccf5abeda0f2993587a7b0bdb6d6766cd00aef40
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0cd594b3c77d7e5ac5be02b4c284c5ad5cd1009c 35e5d2ce273f89af436131c7deaa6f7361e18dc1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0cd594b3c77d7e5ac5be02b4c284c5ad5cd1009c && git merge --no-ff 35e5d2ce273f89af436131c7deaa6f7361e18dc1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0cd594b3c77d7e5ac5be02b4c284c5ad5cd1009c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0cd594b3c77d7e5ac5be02b4c284c5ad5cd1009c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The step-0 report and the 12:42Z split ruling live in project files, not on the card; the PR body's account of Q1/Q2/Q3 is read as a claim, and the tree is judged.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `?package=X` on `GET /meta/:type/:name` for the nine `PACKAGE_SCOPED_READ_TYPES` (app, page, dashboard, report, book, analytics_cube, tool, skill, agent) is the exact qualifier: `admitExactQualifier` admits X when `packageScopedHoldersOf` lists X, when X is a `pairsOf` of a holder, or when a stored row bound to X (active or draft) carries the name; otherwise it throws `not-held-by-qualifier` naming every package holder and the environment's own item; zero holders anywhere stays a miss. `exactQualifierItem` replaces a layer-below answer whose `_packageId` is another installed package by the admitted holder's `getPackageScopedItem`, and refuses two pair bases both holding the name (`ambiguous-in-closure`). RIGHT against ADR-0150 D5 (metadata row: X's item with its bound overlay, or a refusal naming the holders, never X's closure) and against ui carry-in 1: the pair's override row, the pair's added member and the base's item at the pair all keep their answer (pinned in `package-scoped-exact-qualifier.test.ts`, including the base registered second). Types outside the nine keep the prefer-local read, as E8's packageless arm does: RIGHT, the narrowing is scoped to the types whose readers consult (package, name).
2. The new reason `not-held-by-qualifier` widens the published union `PackageScopedRefusalReason` in `@objectstack/core` with its sentence. RIGHT, additive; a consumer switching exhaustively gains a case, which is minor-level.
3. Runtime `domains/meta.ts` rethrows a `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` (or a `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` carrying `refusal.status === 'refused'`) from `getMetaItem` instead of falling through to the by-name `MetadataService.getItem` first match. RIGHT: this is red line 1 made real on the second transport; REST already rendered the 409.
4. New route `GET /meta/:type/:ns/:name` on both transports, `server-only` in both ledgers (the SDK reaches the item by `meta.getItem(type, name, { packageId })`). REST registers it last in `registerMetadataEndpoints`, through the guarded registrar, so the anonymous deny and `metaTypeReadRefusal`/`metaTypeWriteRefusal` wrap it exactly as every other `/meta` route, keyed on `req.params.type`; the route table pin asserts every literal three-segment sibling precedes it, and `RouteManager.register` hands routes to the adapter in registration order. Runtime rewrites a 3-segment GET to the 2-segment item read before the gates, only for a non-anonymous caller, only when `parts[0]` is neither `types` nor `_`-led and `parts[2]` is no sub-resource literal, and only when `resolveMetaItemAddress` answers an address. RIGHT in the main: after the rewrite every gate (type-level read admission, mask posture, query refusal, draft admission, the protocol read's own refusals) judges exactly the read a bare `?package=` would have taken, which is what the qualified read IS; the anonymous deny judges the raw path, so the public-audience exemption (`metaReadRouteOf` answers `item` for two segments only, `book-tree` for `book/:name/tree`) is never reached by a qualified shape on either transport (pinned both sides). No gate is bypassed and no gate is newly satisfied by the rewrite. One accept-set gap in `resolveMetaItemAddress` is WRONG: see ④ finding 1.
5. `_env`: `admitEnvironmentQualifier` refuses a name the environment does not hold when a package does (`callerPackageId: null`, candidates = package holders), for the nine types; otherwise the read is the packageless E8 read. RIGHT against D2/D5 (`_env` names the environment's own item). The REST handler calls it before `readItem`, the runtime inside the item branch after mask posture and query refusal: a transport ordering difference between two refusals (nit, ④ 4).
6. Two qualifiers (`?package=` beside a qualified path) answer 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` on both transports, before the type-read admission on both. RIGHT (no address is picked), with a disclosure nit (④ 3).
7. The sub-resource rule `META_ITEM_SUBRESOURCE_SEGMENTS` (audit, diff, history, layers, publish, published, references, rollback, tree): the runtime checks it before calling and `resolveMetaItemAddress` checks it again, so a last segment in the set never becomes an address on either transport. RIGHT for every literal the runtime ledger serves after `:name` and for every REST three-segment `/meta/:type/:name/LITERAL` and `book/:name/tree`. It omits `bundle` (`GET /api/v1/meta/app/:appId/bundle`, REST only): nit, ④ 2.
8. Activation door `POST /security/_activation/:type/:name`: a thrown package-scoped refusal from the declared-name readers (sharing rule, queue; and now the assignment-rule lookup, which refuses two declaring packages instead of `find`-ing the first) answers 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` with `details.candidates`, writing nothing; one holder and no holder answer as before. RIGHT against the E4 carry-in 6729429263 and red lines 1 and 2. The assignment-rule refusal maps a package-less declaring item to `{ kind: 'environment' }`: consistent with the holder vocabulary.
9. Install door: `installPackage` throws `NamespaceAddressLiteralError` (`NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`, 422, `httpStatus` 422) when `validateNamespaceNotAddressLiteral` (spec/kernel) refuses the namespace, before K's object-name check and with no `collisionPolicy` downgrade. The refused set is derived in spec from `NAMESPACE_POSITION_LITERALS` filtered by `NAMESPACE_PATTERN`: automation `actions`, `connectors`, `hooks`, `trigger`; actions `global`; connectors `oauth` (`_status`, `_activation`, the empty segment and `credential-refs` cannot be a namespace). I recomputed the letter-led literals off the head's runtime `ROUTE_LEDGER` rows under `/automation/`, `/automation/trigger/`, `/automation/hooks/`, `/actions/`, `/automation/connectors/` and `/meta/:type/`: the six match exactly, and the `/meta` namespace position serves no literal. The new conformance test pins the constant against the ledger in both directions. RIGHT. First-party census: no manifest in the tree (`namespace: 'X'` or `"namespace": "X"` for the six, head-wide) declares one of them; the two `namespace: 'global'` hits under `ui/packages/app-shell` are renderer-registry keys, not package manifests; the PR's own CONTROLs install `triggers` and `crm_hooks`. Nothing first-party is refused.
10. `registerMetaItemReadRoutes` now returns the item handler so the qualified route answers through it, never a copy; `MetaDomainProtocol` and the protocol class gain `resolveMetaItemAddress` and `admitEnvironmentQualifier` (canonical-fold roster updated); `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` exports `META_ITEM_SUBRESOURCE_SEGMENTS` and `MetaItemAddress`; `rest-config-mount-table.pin.test.ts` learns that `metadata.endpoints.item` now gates fourteen routes. All RIGHT and additive.
11. Dogfood pin: `PUT /meta/object/views/NAME` (the retired compound save) now answers 405 `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` with `allowed: [GET, HEAD]` for anonymous and member alike, because the shape `/meta/:type/:x/:y` now has one GET route and the adapter's unmatched sink answers a verb mismatch with the verbs the shape serves (HEAD rides GET per `packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts`). RIGHT: no PUT is routed, no auth floor speaks, and the pin keeps asserting anonymous and member get the same answer.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/31691-meta-qualified-address.md`: `minor` for core, objectql, metadata-protocol, rest, runtime; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`; a BREAKING banner listing the four narrowings, the 405 note, a FROM → TO fix for each, and one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines and the same banner; the title carries `!`. Against the diff: the five packages are exactly the released packages the diff moves (qa/dogfood is private; spec, metadata-core and types are read, not moved). AGENTS rule 3: a `narrowed` kind takes at least `minor` on every package the diff moves, so five `minor` is the level the rule yields; `(narrowing)` is BREAKING, so the banner, the FROM → TO fixes and the ADR-0087 marker are owed and present. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is the right kind: the manifest `namespace` is a value an author writes, and six values of it are now refused at install (deviation 1, sound; step 0's `none` was measured before the install refusal was in the part). `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is right for the four published refusals; the qualified read is additive surface inside the same declaration. Check Changeset is `success` on the head. The `Clause-②:` line and the changeset agree with what the tree publishes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Q1 (sub-resource literal in the last position keeps its route; the item so named is reached by `?package=`): answered in the tree on both transports and pinned both ways. Sound as the runtime's reading of D5 step 1. For the ADR-0150 amendment card the list to state is every literal served in the name position of a three-segment `/meta/:type/X/Y` on either transport; the head's set omits REST's `bundle` (④ 2), which the card should carry so the two transports read one rule.
- Q2 (`Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, changeset `minor`): answered, ② above. Sound.
- Q3 (non-GET verbs on `/meta/:type/:x/:y` answer 405 `Allow: GET, HEAD`): answered; keep. The 405 is the adapter's standing contract for any shape that serves another verb (`/meta/:type/:name/history` under PUT already answered it), it runs before the auth floor exactly as the former 404 did, it names only the verbs of a parametric shape that the published route ledger and OpenAPI already disclose, and the pin still asserts anonymous and member get the same answer, which is what #2567 and #12176 D3 guard. Deviation 2 sound; nothing in the spec read forbids it.
- Deviation 3 (REST no-address 404 is the host's `ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND`; the sub-resource rule lives in the protocol): sound. The route answers what the host answered the path before the route existed, through `sendError` so `check:error-code-provenance` and `check:route-envelope` hold, and `@objectstack/rest` reaches the rule as a service (`resolveMetaItemAddress`) rather than importing metadata-protocol. The runtime's own pre-check of `META_ITEM_SUBRESOURCE_SEGMENTS` reads the same constant.
- Names (seat's call): no new error code; `NamespaceAddressLiteralError` reuses `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` 422 as K's error does, which fits the remedy (rename).
- Part (b) carry-in (`/actions` object-less fallback): out of this part; not faulted.
- ui carry-in 2 (Console's bare two-holder read answers 409 on the runtime now): declared in the PR body as a carry-in; this PR changes nothing under `ui/`. The ui lane files the reader card.
- Escalation: the D2 shareable-namespace case below is a finding, not a flag, since the ADR already assigns it to G1.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing is judged against the published spec on main (ADR-0150 D2, D3, D5 and the G1 row of the execution plan). Each of the four declared narrowings makes a refusal the spec itself writes real at the door, and none takes a declared capability away at the consumer: `?package=X` for a name X does not hold was never declared (D5 names it a refusal); the runtime fall-through was a transport defect against a protocol refusal that already existed; the activation door's 503 and first-match were wrong statuses for a refusal the resolver already threw; the six-literal install refusal is D5's own, assigned to G1. Pair reads keep their answer. The gates judge the rewritten path as the read it is, and the anonymous deny judges the raw path on both transports. Trying to break it:

1. MUST-FIX. A qualified address under a shareable namespace with two holders is silently picked. `resolveMetaItemAddress` (protocol-exact-qualifier.ts, the line `const packageId = owners.find(owner in holders) ?? owners[0]`, spelled there with an arrow function) names the first owner that holds the name. Inside a judged namespace that is at most one owner (child N's `refuseNamespaceHolderConflicts`), but N's rule is skipped for `base`, `system` and `sys` (`isNamespaceJudged`, `SHAREABLE_NAMESPACES`), and `installPackage`'s namespace gate also exempts them (`isShareableNamespace`), so two packages of namespace `sys` can each hold `page/home` (the registry admits two holders of a page, as the PR's own fixtures show). `GET /meta/page/sys/home` on either transport then resolves to `?package=FIRST-OWNER`, `admitExactQualifier` admits it (the holder list contains it) and the first owner's item is served 200. ADR-0150 D2 (main, the paragraph accepted in record 6728571147) says of exactly this case: "a qualified address under it does not always name one item. The door then answers 409 with the candidates and never picks; G1 pins that 409." The head neither refuses nor pins it; the PR body's "a namespace two packages co-own names the owner that holds the name" reads D2 without its stated exception. This is red line 2 (ambiguity reported, never guessed) on the new door, and the bare read of the same name already answers 409, so the qualified form is looser than the bare one. Fix: when more than one owner of the namespace holds the name, answer the D3 refusal naming every holder (409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`) instead of picking; render it on both transports (on the runtime the resolve call sits at domain entry outside the item branch's try, so either return a refusing address kind or make sure the throw reaches `dispatch`'s `resolveThrownHttpError` as 409), and pin it (two `sys` packages holding one page: 409 with both candidates; one holder: served). FAIL.
2. NIT. `META_ITEM_SUBRESOURCE_SEGMENTS` omits `bundle`. REST serves `GET /meta/app/:appId/bundle` before the qualified route, so `/meta/app/NS/bundle` is the bundle there; the runtime dispatcher serves no bundle route, so there it is now the qualified read of an app named `bundle` in namespace NS (a miss unless such an app exists), where before it was `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`. No first-party app is named `bundle`; the constant's doc claims it covers "either transport" and the Q1 amendment card should carry the full list. Fix on the amendment card or as a follow-up; a code change here moves the head.
3. NIT. On both transports the two-qualifier 400 and the no-address 404 are answered before the type-level read admission, so an authenticated caller who may not read the type learns whether a middle segment is an installed namespace. Anonymous callers are denied first, namespaces are the public address vocabulary D2 chose, and the two transports agree; recorded, not graded higher.
4. NIT. Refusal precedence differs for `_env` with a malformed query: REST calls `admitEnvironmentQualifier` before `readItem`'s query recognition, so `/meta/page/_env/solo?bogus=1` on a package-held name answers 409 there and 400 on the runtime (query refusal first). Both are refusals of the same request; no item is served. Follow-up at most.
5. Tried and held: an anonymous qualified or `_env` read of a public-audience type (book, doc) is denied 401 on both transports before the address is read (pinned both sides); the rewrite happens only for GET and only for a non-anonymous caller, so no write gate, save verdict or type-write admission sees a rewritten path; a pair read keeps its answer when another package registered the name first and when the pair holds a draft or active row; `?package=all` beside a qualified path is the 400, consistent with `metaItemPackageBinding`; a `_`-led middle segment other than `_env` and an uninstalled namespace answer the pre-existing 404 on both transports; the six refused literals equal the letter-led ledger literals and no first-party manifest spells one; the route order on REST is registration order and the qualified route is last among `/meta`; the 405 alters no auth floor and discloses no item.

Delta review of record 6744488933 (head eabb8e3a0, FAIL, one must-fix). One commit, 40a88d88, no merge, no rebase.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The must-fix is closed.** `resolveMetaItemAddress` now keeps the namespace's owners that hold the name. More than one throws `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` with the new reason `ambiguous-in-namespace`, `callerPackageId: null`, and every holding owner as a candidate. The sentence says nothing picks one. One holder is served, and no holder still names the first owner so the exact read answers its own miss. This is ADR-0150 D2 (line 102 on main): the address answers 409 with the candidates and never picks. Right.
2. **Both transports render it as 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`.** On REST, the throw lands in the qualified route's existing catch. On the runtime, the resolve call is now in its own try at domain entry and answers through `errorFromThrown(e, 409)`. Pinned on both: two `sys` owners holding `page/home` answer 409 naming both, and a CONTROL with one holder answers 200 with its item. The reported ablation (refusal off, first holder taken) is red in each file, and the CONTROL stays green. Right.
3. **The new reason widens `PackageScopedRefusalReason`** in `@objectstack/core` with its sentence. This is additive and inside core's declared `minor`. Right.

### ② Semver level

**What passes**
- **The exact qualifier (D5, ruling 6724570466).** `?package=X` and `/meta/:type/:ns/:name` answer X's item (a `.custom` pair answers its base's items and its own added members) or refuse, naming the holders. - **Shareable namespaces.** When two `sys`/`base`/`system` holders hold the name, the answer is 409 with the candidates, never a pick. This is pinned on both transports and fixes the contract-review must-fix.
- **The runtime dispatcher** no longer falls through to the by-name service read after the protocol refuses. Activation answers 409 with `details.candidates` and writes nothing. That closes the G1 carry-in from E4 (6729429263).
- **R's vocabulary.** The two new refusal reasons in `@objectstack/core` (`not-held-by-qualifier`, `ambiguous-in-namespace`) only add to the type. The rule itself is unchanged. They are fine in R's file.
- **Breaking items.** Items 1 to 3 and the 405 are declared FROM→TO, with a first-party count of 0.

**R1 (required): an already-installed package whose namespace is an address literal must not stop the boot.**
`validateNamespaceNotAddressLiteral` runs in `registerPackage`. That is the install gate, and it is also the re-registration path every boot takes for every installed package. Nothing on main refuses these six namespaces today; P #31765 only declared the grammar. So a deployment that already has a package with namespace `global`, `hooks`, `trigger`, `oauth`, `actions` or `connectors` would fail its next boot after upgrading, with 422 `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`. The changeset says "refused at install", and it does not mention that boot failure. The first-party count of 0 does not cover customer installs.

Fix, at the root:
- **A new install** of such a namespace is refused with 422, as written.
- **A package already installed** under it keeps booting. Use the namespace gate's own "same-package reinstall/reload" reading to tell the two cases apart.
  - It warns once, naming the namespace and the route that shadows it.
  - Its qualified path is unreachable, so it is read with `?package=`.
  - It is named in the upgrade report: S4's `os migrate stored-references` report, or the D10 report section.
- **Pin both cases:** a fresh install refused, and a pre-existing install re-registered at boot that warns and still serves `?package=`. Run the boot pin with the exemption ablated (red), then with it (green).
- **In the changeset,** state the case split.

If the seat would rather refuse the boot, the changeset must say so plainly, with the remedy (rename the namespace before upgrading), and B/S4 would owe a pre-upgrade check. I recommend the exemption, because a namespace that a route shadows loses only its qualified path, which never existed before this PR.
